$why: A FRAGMENT of guard-vocabulary, 2026-08-15. It appears only when there is a repository
index to verify against; with none, the parent prompt must not carry a heading implying
the agent can check something it cannot.
It is its own template rather than a string in code because the rule is that EVERY prompt
lives in the template layer — a conditional section is still prompt text, and putting it
in a helper would have quietly re-created the thing this migration removes.
The leading newline lives HERE, not in the parent. Put in the parent it produced a blank
line in exactly the branch where no index exists — visible only in the case with no
evidence, which is the case least likely to be looked at.
body:
VERIFY BEFORE YOU ANSWER — you have a real index of this repository.

  PROJECT_ROOT="__REPO_PATH__" bash "__CODEGRAPH_TOOL__" query <SymbolName>
  PROJECT_ROOT="__REPO_PATH__" bash "__CODEGRAPH_TOOL__" explore <terms>

Run it via Bash. A candidate term that resolves to NOTHING in this index is noise and
belongs in the blacklist, however unusual the word looks. Do not assert that a term is
meaningful — check it.

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE: the list you return feeds a BM25/IDF ranker. That ranker DEMOTES
terms which are common in the corpus and AMPLIFIES terms which are rare. So a rare,
meaningless token — a bracketed brand tag, a ticket label, a person's name — is not
diluted, it is promoted to a top discriminator and drags the search away from the real
code. Rare-and-meaningless is the failure mode you exist to prevent; do not mistake
rarity for signal.
description: Told to the guard-vocabulary agent only when a CodeGraph index exists to verify terms against.
